prompt: What does Collections.sort(list) do to an ArrayList<Integer>?
choices: Returns a new sorted list, leaving the original unchanged
Sorts the list in-place in ascending natural order
Sorts the list in descending order
explanation: Collections.sort() sorts the list in-place in natural (ascending) order. For descending: Collections.sort(list, Collections.reverseOrder()). Java 8+: list.sort(Comparator.naturalOrder()); is equivalent.
